>Adler — treino de leitura de casos de abuso<

Adler é um utilitário open source de treinamento, pensado para ensinar os casos de abuso de um fluxo sob diferentes perspectivas — para os times de ideação e desenvolvimento de produtos, processos e fluxos. Cada caso é um fluxo de negócio real: você analisa o contexto, marca o que considera arriscado e depois compara com os riscos reais — técnicos, de lógica de negócio, operacionais e regulatórios —, cada um com o caso de abuso, o impacto e a mitigação.

Adler is an open source training tool, built to teach the abuse cases of a flow from different perspectives — for the teams that ideate and build products, processes and flows. Each case is a real business flow: you study the context, mark what you think is risky and then compare it with the real risks — technical, business logic, operational and regulatory —, each with its abuse case, impact and mitigation.
Um negócio real com atores, dados e fluxos. Nada de "corp fictícia com um endpoint".
A real business with actors, data and flows. No "fictional corp with one endpoint".
Um diagrama do fluxo transacional. Onde os dados nascem, atravessam, descansam.
A diagram of the transactional flow. Where data is born, travels and rests.
Você marca tudo que suspeita — técnico, lógica, operativo, regulatório. Sem gabarito à mostra.
You mark everything you suspect — technical, business logic, operational, regulatory. No answer key in sight.
O que era, a categoria de risco, o caso de abuso concreto, o impacto, a mitigação.
What it was, the risk category, the concrete abuse case, the impact, the mitigation.
O que você pegou, o que passou batido e os padrões para levar ao próximo caso.
What you caught, what you missed and the patterns to take to the next case.
Os casos são independentes; a ordem só ajuda quem está começando.
Cases are independent; the order only helps if you're starting out.

Leia como se estivesse chegando ao squad amanhã. Não é hora de julgar — é hora de entender o que a empresa vende, para quem e como o dinheiro se move.
Read it as if you were joining the squad tomorrow. It's not time to judge — it's time to understand what the company sells, to whom, and how the money moves.
Onde os dados nascem, por onde passam, onde ficam parados. Fronteiras de confiança em destaque — é ali que os problemas geralmente moram.
Where data is born, where it passes, where it sits. Trust boundaries are highlighted — that's usually where the problems live.
↔ Arraste o diagrama para o lado para ver o fluxo inteiro.
↔ Drag the diagram sideways to see the whole flow.
Clique num sistema (ou use Tab e Enter) para ver o que ele faz e com quem troca dados.
Click a system (or use Tab and Enter) to see what it does and who it exchanges data with.

Marque tudo que parecer um risco — de segurança, privacidade, fraude ou lógica de negócio. Alguns itens são armadilhas plausíveis: parte do treino é saber por que uma preocupação é ou não é o problema aqui.
Mark everything that looks like a risk — security, privacy, fraud or business logic. Some items are plausible traps: part of the practice is knowing why a concern is or isn't the problem here.
Leitura já revelada. As marcações ficam travadas depois da revelação, para que a resposta não mude depois de ver o gabarito.
Reading already revealed. Marks are locked after the reveal, so the answer can't change after seeing the key.
Os riscos reais — o que se vê no contexto, os casos de abuso concretos, o impacto e como se resolve. Cada risco carrega a lente que devia tê-lo pegado primeiro.
The real risks — what shows in the context, the concrete abuse cases, the impact and how to fix it. Each risk carries the lens that should have caught it first.
>Where each risk lives in the flow<
Clique num número para ir ao risco, ou num sistema para ver os riscos que moram nele. Passe o mouse num risco, aqui ou nos cards abaixo, para ver por onde ele passa.
Click a number to jump to the risk, or a system to see the risks that live in it. Hover over a risk, here or in the cards below, to see where it runs.
↔ Arraste o mapa para o lado para ver todos os riscos.
↔ Drag the map sideways to see every risk.
Cabe menos ao número e mais ao padrão: onde sua leitura pegou o movimento, onde passou batido, e o que levar para o próximo caso.
It's less about the number and more about the pattern: where your reading caught the move, where it missed, and what to take to the next case.
Take it to the next one
Um caso é um objeto JSON. Todo o motor lê essa estrutura — não há código específico por caso. Se você conhece um cenário de negócio interessante, você já sabe escrever um.
A case is a JSON object. The whole engine reads that structure — there's no case-specific code. If you know an interesting business scenario, you already know how to write one.
Identificador URL-safe. Aparece na navegação e no progresso salvo.
URL-safe identifier. Shows up in navigation and in saved progress.
Setor do caso — fintech, marketplace, healthtech, edtech, govtech. Ajuda a categorizar; não muda a lógica.
The case's sector — fintech, marketplace, healthtech, edtech, govtech. Helps categorize; doesn't change the logic.
Parágrafos do briefing. O primeiro parágrafo é destacado como lede.
Briefing paragraphs. The first one is highlighted as the lede.
Listas de pares chave-valor para a barra lateral. Curtas, específicas, escritas com os termos que o negócio realmente usa.
Lists of key-value pairs for the sidebar. Short, specific, written with the terms the business actually uses.

Nós e arestas do diagrama. Cada nó tem kind (interno, fronteira, terceiro), que colore o quadro, icon (API, banco de dados, fila, parceiro…), que mostra o que o sistema é, e description, o texto que aparece quando a pessoa clica no sistema.

Nodes and edges of the diagram. Each node has a kind (internal, boundary, third party), which colours the box, an icon (API, database, queue, partner…), which shows what the system is, and a description, the text shown when someone clicks the system.
Todas as opções que aparecem na leitura. Cada uma marca category (técnico, lógica, operativo, processo, regulatório, privacidade, fraude) e truth (real ou distrator).

Every option shown in the reading. Each one sets a category (the schema values are in Portuguese: técnico, lógica, operativo, processo, regulatório, privacidade, fraude) and truth (real or distractor).

Só os itens reais. Cada risco tem: título, category, severity, signal (pistas no contexto), abuse (casos de abuso), impact, mitigation e where: os nós e arestas do fluxo onde o risco mora, que viram o mapa de riscos da revelação.

Only the real items. Each risk has a title, category, severity, signal (clues in the context), abuse (abuse cases), impact, mitigation and where: the nodes and edges of the flow where the risk lives, which become the reveal's risk map.
Três a cinco padrões generalizáveis. Não é resumo — é o que a pessoa carrega para o próximo caso.
Three to five patterns that generalize. Not a summary — it's what people carry to the next case.

Abra um pull request em github.com/2T0nnks/baker-street com o seu JSON em cases/. O CI valida o schema automaticamente e a revisão editorial olha realismo, distratores e mitigações. O passo a passo está em docs/CONTRIBUTING.md. Quem tem um caso aprovado entra como Irregular.

Open a pull request at github.com/2T0nnks/baker-street with your JSON in cases/. CI validates the schema automatically and the editorial review looks at realism, distractors and mitigations. The step-by-step guide (in Portuguese) is in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md; an English version of a case goes in cases/en/. Anyone with an approved case becomes an Irregular.
Adler treina o olhar que só se afia contra um adversário.
Adler trains the eye that only sharpens against an adversary.
Homenagem a Irene Adler, a única a superar Sherlock Holmes — porque o leu antes que ele a lesse. É esse o olhar que Adler treina: identificar os casos de abuso de um produto antes de ele existir.
A tribute to Irene Adler, the only one to outwit Sherlock Holmes — because she read him before he read her. That's the eye Adler trains: spotting a product's abuse cases before it exists.

Frameworks descrevem princípios: minimização de dados, menor privilégio, defesa em profundidade. O que raramente treinam é o momento clínico — o funcionário júnior lendo uma RFC e percebendo que o campo ownerId nunca aparece no filtro do endpoint. Adler é para esse momento.

Frameworks describe principles: data minimization, least privilege, defence in depth. What they rarely train is the clinical moment — the junior employee reading an RFC and noticing that the ownerId field never shows up in the endpoint's filter. Adler is for that moment.
É especialmente útil para onboarding cruzado: quando times diferentes discutem o mesmo caso — produto, engenharia, tesouraria, antifraude, compliance — ficam claros os pontos cegos de cada área.
It's especially useful for cross-team onboarding: when different teams discuss the same case — product, engineering, treasury, fraud prevention, compliance — each area's blind spots become clear.

Rode um caso por sessão de 60–90 minutos. Cada pessoa percorre o caso no próprio navegador e marca sua leitura sozinha, sem conversar. Depois, abram a revelação juntos e comparem quem marcou o quê, categoria por categoria (técnico, lógica, operativo, regulatório). As divergências entre áreas são o material mais rico da discussão: cada uma enxerga casos de abuso diferentes no mesmo fluxo.

Run one case per 60–90 minute session. Each person goes through the case in their own browser and marks their reading alone, without talking. Then open the reveal together and compare who marked what, category by category (technical, business logic, operational, regulatory). The disagreements between areas are the richest material for discussion: each one sees different abuse cases in the same flow.
Cada risco revelado já vem no formato de threat model: casos de abuso × mitigação — a mesma estrutura usada em RFCs de fluxos transacionais.
Each revealed risk already comes in threat model form: abuse cases × mitigation — the same structure used in RFCs for transactional flows.

nodeTech.user: A person who uses the system directly — customer, operator or partner. Their actions enter the flow through an interface such as an app, a website or a support channel.
nodeTech.app: An app installed on the user's phone. It runs on a device the company doesn't control: everything it sends reaches the server as requests over the internet.
nodeTech.web: An application accessed through the browser. The page is delivered by the server and runs on the visitor's computer; every action becomes an HTTP request to an API.
nodeTech.api: API (application programming interface): a set of addresses, the endpoints, that receive requests — usually HTTP with JSON — and send back responses. It's how apps, websites and other systems talk to the back end.
nodeTech.service: Back-end service: a program running on the company's servers that carries out part of the business logic, with no user interface. It talks to other systems through APIs or queues.
nodeTech.database: Database: where records are stored in a structured way (tables, rows and columns) and queried by other systems, usually with SQL.
nodeTech.storage: Object storage (such as an S3 bucket) or physical storage: keeps whole items — files, videos, media — identified by a name. Access is controlled by policies on who can read, write or list.
nodeTech.queue: Message queue: one system publishes events and another consumes them later, at its own pace. This decouples both sides; if the consumer fails, the message can be delivered again.
nodeTech.webhook: Webhook: an address that an external system calls — usually with an HTTP POST — to report that something happened, such as a confirmed payment. The caller takes the initiative, not the receiver.
nodeTech.payment: Payment method: the system that actually moves the money — card, PIX (Brazil's instant payments), boleto — and reports whether the transaction was approved and settled.
nodeTech.bank: An institution or infrastructure of the financial system that holds balances and settles transactions, regulated by the Central Bank.
nodeTech.partner: Third party: another company's system, integrated into the flow by contract and API. The company doesn't control how it works inside — only what it sends and what it gets back.
nodeTech.team: People operating the system, usually through a back office: an internal application with permissions to view and change data that customers can't change on their own.
nodeTech.ai: An artificial intelligence model that generates or classifies content from an input. The result is probabilistic: it can vary from one run to the next and it can be wrong.
nodeTech.document: A document generated by the system — PDF, contract, receipt —, often digitally signed, which proves who issued it and that the content hasn't been changed.
nodeTech.spreadsheet: A spreadsheet or tabular file (Excel, Google Sheets, CSV) used for tracking or exchanging data outside the main systems.
nodeTech.email: An asynchronous message channel — email, SMS, notification — that carries information to people or to other systems.
nodeTech.audit: Audit record (log): notes who did what and when, for investigation and compliance.
nodeTech.key: HSM (Hardware Security Module): a dedicated device that generates and stores cryptographic keys and operates with them — signing, encrypting, decrypting — without the private key ever leaving the hardware. It is certified to resist physical tampering.
